newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends thinly traded session higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures settled moderately higher in sluggish dealings Wednesday, boosted by light industry and speculative buying, floor sources said.
But scale-up selling by the trade capped gains, they added, confining prices to a narrow range and preventing a test of near-term resistance at $1,350 basis the active March contract.
March delivery rose $9 a tonne on the day, to $1,347, after ranging between $1,349 to $1,341. Second-month May also gained $9 to close at $1,370, while the back months finished up $8 to $10.

On the charts, traders pegged March's next resistance at $1,359, then $1,370. Support was seen at $1,331, a double bottom on the charts. The next downside target was put near $1,322, March's life-of-contract low.
"There is not a lot going on in this market and the volume has not been great," one trader said. "We are really stuck in a range."
Fundamentally, Ghana cocoa buyers expected arrivals to pick up from January after late rains, with output seen closer to 350,000 tonnes.
Traders said the market was likely to stay in a range between $1,320 and $1,400 basis March, with steady manufacturer interest near the lows and persistant origin selling toward the highs.
They await the U.S. fourth quarter cocoa grind data due Friday at 0845 EST. Industry sources expected grindings to rise three to five percent compared with the 1995 fourth quarter grind figures.
